official_syllabus_verbatim: Rationalism (Descartes, Spinoza, Leibniz); Cartesian Method and Certain Knowledge; Substance; God; Mind-Body Dualism; Determinism and Freedom.

core_sessions.title: Rationalist Project: Reason, Certainty and the 3-1-Infinity Sequence
core_sessions.plain: Rationalism treats reason as capable of reaching necessary structure, yet Descartes, Spinoza and Leibniz produce rival ontologies.
core_sessions.technical: Early-modern rationalism privileges a priori principles, intellectual intuition and deduction while using substance metaphysics to explain knowledge, God, mind, body and freedom.
core_sessions.answer: Rationalism is unified by confidence in a priori reason but divided by the criterion of substance, which moves from Cartesian dualism through Spinozist monism to Leibnizian monadic pluralism.
core_sessions.usage: Open with a priori reason, intuition and deduction; then use the substance 3-1-infinity sequence to show how each successor answers Cartesian dualism.
core_sessions.mechanism: A shared demand for intelligibility produces different systems because independence, simplicity and individuation are interpreted differently.
core_sessions.consequence: The trio is a dialectical sequence rather than three disconnected lives.
core_sessions.trap: Do not define rationalism as rejection of all experience or assume that a shared method entails one doctrine of substance, God or freedom.
core_sessions.objection: Three incompatible systems may suggest that reason alone underdetermines metaphysics.
core_sessions.reply: Shared standards do not decide which first principles and substance criteria are correct.
core_sessions.limit: The reply preserves rationalism's family resemblance but supplies no neutral procedure for choosing the final system.
core_sessions.exam: Use methodological unity plus ontological divergence; never write a generic school summary when the question names one philosopher.
revision: Reason supplies necessity and universality; sensation may occasion thought.
Substance sequence: Descartes 3, Spinoza 1, Leibniz indefinitely many.
Mind-body sequence: interactionism, parallelism, pre-established harmony.

core_sessions.title: Descartes I: Methodic Doubt, Cogito and Certain Knowledge
core_sessions.plain: Descartes suspends every belief that can fail until the act of doubting reveals an indubitable thinking existence.
core_sessions.technical: Methodological doubt moves through sense error, the dream argument and the evil-genius hypothesis to the cogito, an immediate intuition that grounds a foundationalist order of intuition and deduction.
core_sessions.answer: The cogito defeats radical doubt performatively: deception may falsify what is thought, but it cannot erase the occurrence and existence of the thinker while thinking.
core_sessions.usage: Move from methodological doubt and the dream and evil-genius tests to the cogito, then distinguish intuition, deduction and foundationalism from a proof of enduring substance.
core_sessions.mechanism: The attempt to doubt thinking existence performs the very thinking whose existence it tries to deny.
core_sessions.consequence: Self-knowledge gains epistemic priority, while world, God and enduring personal identity still require reconstruction.
core_sessions.trap: Do not call the cogito a syllogism or say that it alone proves an immortal soul.
core_sessions.objection: The Lichtenberg-style objection says that Descartes establishes only 'there is thinking,' not a substantial 'I'.
core_sessions.reply: A Cartesian reply is that modes of thinking require a subject, although this already invokes the substance framework.
core_sessions.limit: The cogito is strongest as local first-person certainty and weaker as an unaided proof of enduring immaterial substance.
core_sessions.exam: For certainty questions, separate the indubitability of present thinking from the mediated knowledge of world and memory.
revision: Doubt is methodological, hyperbolic and temporary.
Sequence: senses, dream, evil genius, cogito.
Clear and distinct perception takes the cogito as its model.

core_sessions.title: Descartes II: Ideas, God, Reconstruction and the Cartesian Circle
core_sessions.plain: After the cogito, Descartes uses ideas and proofs of a non-deceiving God to extend certainty beyond the immediately attended thought.
core_sessions.technical: The reconstruction distinguishes innate, adventitious and factitious ideas, uses causal adequacy and ontological reasoning for God, invokes divine veracity, and restores clear and distinct perception, mathematics and an external extended world.
core_sessions.answer: God is the epistemic hinge of Cartesian reconstruction because divine non-deception extends clear and distinct certainty beyond the cogito, yet that hinge creates the Cartesian Circle.
core_sessions.usage: Order innate ideas, divine veracity and clear and distinct perception around the Cartesian Circle, then qualify the memory-guarantee reply.
core_sessions.mechanism: A perfect non-deceiving God is used to guarantee that what is clearly and distinctly perceived remains trustworthy beyond immediate attention.
core_sessions.consequence: Mathematics and res extensa return, but the system inherits the burden of its divine proofs and their epistemic premises.
core_sessions.trap: Do not say that the wax proves the external world; it shows that body, if known, is grasped intellectually as extended and changeable.
core_sessions.objection: Descartes seems to trust clear and distinct premises to prove God and then trust God to validate those premises.
core_sessions.reply: The standard reply distinguishes present compelled intuition from remembered or extended reasoning, for which divine veracity is needed.
core_sessions.limit: The reply narrows the circle but remains contested because the proofs of God themselves contain extended inferential steps.
core_sessions.exam: Use architecture rather than a list: criterion, proof, guarantee, reconstruction, objection, reply and residual difficulty.
revision: Ideas are classed as innate, adventitious and factitious.
God guarantees non-deceptive clear and distinct cognition.
The world-proof establishes material cause more securely than sensible detail.

core_sessions.title: Descartes III: Substance, Dualism, Interaction and Freedom
core_sessions.plain: Descartes distinguishes thinking and extended created substances while making both continuously dependent on infinite substance, God.
core_sessions.technical: Res cogitans has thought as principal attribute and mental states as modes; res extensa has extension as principal attribute and shapes or motions as modes. Their real distinction grounds interactionist dualism.
core_sessions.answer: Cartesian dualism gains conceptual clarity by separating thought from extension, but its success in distinction becomes its central causal problem because heterogeneous substances must still explain one life.
core_sessions.usage: Define substance, attribute and mode before presenting real distinction, interaction, objections, and Descartes' account of error and freedom.
core_sessions.mechanism: Clear and distinct conceivability supports real distinction, while the human union is treated as a primitive lived fact rather than a third substance.
core_sessions.consequence: The theory protects mental irreducibility and free judgement but faces interaction, causal-closure, other-minds and personhood pressures.
core_sessions.trap: Do not count God, mind and body as three co-equal substances: only God is absolutely independent.
core_sessions.objection: Princess Elisabeth asks how an unextended mind can causally alter an extended body without a shared causal medium.
core_sessions.reply: Descartes appeals to the primitive notion of mind-body union and embodied experience rather than reducing union to pure thought or extension.
core_sessions.limit: This protects phenomenological unity but does not supply a transparent mechanism compatible with physical causal closure.
core_sessions.exam: Compare real distinction with substantial union and separate rational freedom of judgement from mere indifference.
revision: Substance bears attributes; modes are changing determinations.
Mind is unextended and thinking; body is extended and non-thinking.
Error occurs when will outruns clear intellectual perception.

LIMIT: a primitive notion is not a detailed causal mechanism

core_sessions.title: Spinoza I: One Substance, Attributes, Modes and Immanent God
core_sessions.plain: Spinoza applies the independence criterion strictly and turns Cartesian mind and body from substances into expressions of one reality.
core_sessions.technical: The self-caused, necessarily existing and absolutely infinite substance is Deus sive Natura; infinitely many attributes express its essence, while finite things are modes under attributes such as Thought and Extension.
core_sessions.answer: Spinoza radicalises the Cartesian definition of substance until only God or Nature remains self-conceived, making minds and bodies dependent modes rather than independently interacting things.
core_sessions.usage: Derive monism from strict independence, distinguish attributes from modes, and qualify pantheism by noting that God is not merely the aggregate of finite things.
core_sessions.mechanism: Because substance is conceived through itself and cannot be limited by another substance of the same nature, the system culminates in one infinite substance.
core_sessions.consequence: Creator-world dualism disappears, but individuality and divine personality become difficult.
core_sessions.trap: Do not treat Thought and Extension as two Spinozist substances or interpret 'in God' as spatial containment.
core_sessions.objection: The acosmism objection claims that if God alone is absolutely real, finite individuals dissolve.
core_sessions.reply: Spinoza can retain dependent modal reality: finite beings are not nothing, but determinate expressions without self-subsistence.
core_sessions.limit: Dependent reality remains weaker than robust individuality and personal divine agency.
core_sessions.exam: For pantheism questions, define the exact identity, explain immanence, then address aggregate and acosmism objections.
revision: Whatever is, is in God as substance or mode.
Humans know Thought and Extension, not all infinite attributes.
God is immanent cause, not a transcendent artisan.

core_sessions.title: Spinoza II: Parallelism, Necessity, Conatus and Freedom
core_sessions.plain: Spinoza replaces interaction with two descriptions of one order and redefines freedom as acting through adequate understanding.
core_sessions.technical: The order and connection of ideas is the same as the order and connection of things; causal necessity governs all modes, conatus expresses each thing's striving, and adequate ideas convert passive bondage into rational activity.
core_sessions.answer: Spinoza reconciles freedom with determinism by treating freedom not as uncaused choice but as adequate self-determination within the necessary order of God or Nature.
core_sessions.usage: Explain parallelism first, derive necessity from substance, then show how conatus and adequate knowledge permit relative freedom and liberation.
core_sessions.mechanism: The same modal event is expressed under Thought as an idea and under Extension as a body-state, eliminating cross-attribute causal transfer.
core_sessions.consequence: Causal unity and psychophysical correspondence are secured, while alternative possibilities and retributive responsibility are revised.
core_sessions.trap: Do not confuse parallelism with two independent synchronized substances or freedom with resignation to fate.
core_sessions.objection: Necessitarianism appears to eliminate responsibility, novelty and the ability to do otherwise.
core_sessions.reply: Spinoza shifts responsibility toward causes, character and rational transformation; freedom measures activity from one's understood nature.
core_sessions.limit: The account offers autonomy without alternative possibilities and is therefore compatibilist only in a revisionary sense.
core_sessions.exam: Use metaphysics-parallelism-affects-knowledge-freedom; distinguish necessity from fatalism and passive compulsion.
revision: Parallelism is identity of order under different attributes.
Conatus is the striving to persevere in being.
Adequate ideas increase action; inadequate ideas mark passive bondage.

NO mind-to-body or body-to-mind causal crossing

core_sessions.title: Leibniz I: Monads, Perception, Appetition and Individuality
core_sessions.plain: Leibniz restores plurality through simple, non-extended centres whose changes arise from internal perception and striving.
core_sessions.technical: Monads are windowless, partless and non-extended substances with perception and appetition; their hierarchy ranges from bare monads through animal souls and rational spirits to God as the necessary supreme monad.
core_sessions.answer: Leibniz makes substance simple and active: each monad is a unique perspectival centre whose internally unfolding perceptions preserve individuality without material parts or causal influx.
core_sessions.usage: Derive monads from the inadequacy of divisible extension, explain the hierarchy, and distinguish perception from conscious apperception.
core_sessions.mechanism: Appetition moves each monad from one perception to another according to its own law, while its perspective differentiates it from every other monad.
core_sessions.consequence: Plurality and internal activity return, but material bodies become well-founded phenomena rather than ultimate substances.
core_sessions.trap: Do not describe monads as tiny physical atoms located inside bodies.
core_sessions.objection: A windowless monad seems insulated from evidence about the common world and other minds.
core_sessions.reply: Each monad represents the whole universe from a distinct perspective, with correspondence guaranteed by harmony.
core_sessions.limit: Representation without interaction shifts rather than removes the demand for explaining shared objectivity.
core_sessions.exam: Link simplicity, perception, appetition, hierarchy and individuation before moving to harmony or freedom.
revision: Monads are simple, unextended and windowless.
Perception represents multiplicity in unity; apperception is reflective awareness.
Appetition is the internal principle of transition.

visuals.title: Leibniz's monad hierarchy
visuals.caption: Degrees of perceptual clarity and reason differentiate monads, not physical size or composition.
lines: GOD: NECESSARY SUPREME MONAD / COMPLETE INTELLIGENCE
RATIONAL SPIRITS: apperception, reason, moral agency
ANIMAL SOULS: memory + clearer perception
BARE MONADS: obscure perception / petites perceptions
EACH LEVEL: simple + non-extended + perception + appetition

core_sessions.title: Leibniz II: Harmony, God, Sufficient Reason and Freedom
core_sessions.plain: Pre-established harmony is Leibniz's doctrine that independently unfolding monadic sequences correspond without causal interaction.
core_sessions.technical: Pre-established harmony, the Principle of Sufficient Reason, truths of reason and fact, possible worlds and divine selection support a compatibilism of spontaneity, intelligence and contingency.
core_sessions.answer: Leibniz preserves freedom by distinguishing certainty from absolute necessity: rational actions arise spontaneously from the agent's own reasons, which incline without necessitating in the logical sense.
core_sessions.usage: Explain pre-established harmony through sufficient reason, truths of reason and fact, possible worlds, spontaneity and compatibilism.
core_sessions.mechanism: God chooses a compossible world and creates monads whose internally lawful sequences correspond without causal exchange.
core_sessions.consequence: Coordination, individuality and rational agency coexist, but explanatory economy and the problem of evil become acute.
core_sessions.trap: Do not confuse certainty in the actual world with logical necessity or claim that harmony permits causal messages between monads.
core_sessions.objection: If every predicate belongs to a complete concept and God selected this world, agency may look programmed and evil divinely chosen.
core_sessions.reply: Leibniz distinguishes necessary truths from contingent truths known by infinite analysis and treats reasons as inclining without coercion.
core_sessions.limit: The account secures intelligent self-expression better than libertarian alternative possibilities and does not dissolve evil's moral force.
core_sessions.exam: For freedom questions, state spontaneity, intelligence and contingency, then test whether possible-world alternatives belong to this actual agent.
revision: Harmony coordinates without interaction.
PSR asks why this world and event rather than another.
Truths of reason are necessary; truths of fact are contingent though certain.

NO WINDOWS; NO CROSS-SUBSTANCE CAUSAL INFLUX

core_sessions.title: Comparative Synthesis: Substance, God, Mind-Body and Freedom
core_sessions.plain: The three systems answer the same questions by changing what counts as substance and how causation, individuality and necessity are understood.
core_sessions.technical: The comparison aligns Cartesian created-substance dualism and interactionism, Spinozist substance monism and parallelism, and Leibnizian monadic pluralism and pre-established harmony, with distinct divine and freedom models.
core_sessions.answer: Spinoza removes the interaction gap by collapsing Cartesian substances into attributes of one order, while Leibniz restores plurality by replacing interaction with divinely coordinated internal activity.
core_sessions.usage: Compare substance pluralism, monism and monadic pluralism, then align interactionism, parallelism, harmony, autonomy and compatibilism.
core_sessions.mechanism: Each successor accepts the Cartesian pressure but redistributes substance and causation to avoid direct interaction between heterogeneous realities.
core_sessions.consequence: Explanatory unity rises from Descartes to Spinoza, while Leibniz restores individuality at the cost of a more elaborate theological harmony.
core_sessions.trap: Do not use substance, attribute, mode, mind, body, necessity, determinism, spontaneity, autonomy and freedom as interchangeable terms.
core_sessions.objection: All three solutions may seem to relocate rather than solve the relation between lived agency and a fully intelligible order.
core_sessions.reply: Their lasting value is diagnostic: they isolate interaction, identity, causal explanation and autonomy as distinct problems.
core_sessions.limit: Contemporary relevance should be stated as conceptual inheritance, not as proof that early-modern metaphysics anticipated modern science.
core_sessions.exam: Use one comparison matrix plus a pressure-response paragraph; chronology without common axes will not answer a comparative directive.
revision: Descartes distinguishes; Spinoza unifies; Leibniz pluralizes without interaction.
God guarantees, is immanent reality, or selects and coordinates.
Freedom becomes will, understood necessity, or intelligent spontaneity.

core_sessions.title: Criticism-Reply Map, Precision Toolkit and Answer Spine
core_sessions.plain: A high-scoring answer reconstructs an argument, identifies its strongest pressure, gives the best reply and states what remains unresolved.
core_sessions.technical: The examiner-grade method distinguishes epistemic from ontological claims, necessity from determinism, spontaneity from autonomy, and compatibility from libertarian freedom before directive-specific evaluation.
core_sessions.answer: A criticism-reply answer spine reveals rationalism's central tension: systematic intelligibility repeatedly pressures interaction, contingency and autonomous individuality.
core_sessions.usage: Use argument reconstruction and directive fidelity to build a claim-evidence-analysis-qualification answer spine with objection, reply and qualified verdict.
core_sessions.mechanism: Precision turns system summaries into answers by linking every doctrine to a named inferential role and an explicit qualification.
core_sessions.consequence: The same master map can answer narrow questions on God, substance, mind-body or freedom without collapsing into a generic history of rationalism.
core_sessions.trap: Do not invent quotations, present contested interpretations as fact, or append an unrelated criticism after the conclusion.
core_sessions.objection: A compressed comparison can flatten differences in text, purpose and degree of necessity.
core_sessions.reply: Use common axes only after each concept has been independently defined and the comparison qualified.
core_sessions.limit: No matrix substitutes for the argument demanded by the exact PYQ directive.
core_sessions.exam: Answer spine: direct thesis, definitions, numbered argument, named example, objection, reply, residual limitation and directive-specific verdict.
revision: Distinguish independence, attribute and mode before counting substances.
Distinguish causal necessity, hypothetical necessity and logical necessity.
End with a qualified judgement, not a slogan that one thinker simply wins.
